title: Microsoft Outlook 和 OpenAI 的 ChatGPT Work 遇到用户中断
content:
长期合作伙伴 OpenAI 和微软均表示，周一他们的关键产品出现了中断，但没有相关报告。

OpenAI 表示，其企业人工智能代理 ChatGPT Work 的错误率和延迟已持续约三个小时。微软表示，Exchange Online 存在问题。“多个订阅计划的用户可能无法在 ChatGPT Work 中启动或继续任务，”OpenAI 在其状态页面上表示。 “我们正在继续努力实施缓解措施。” 截至下午 2:24美国东部时间周一，超过 1,100 名用户在 DownDetector（一个跟踪中断的网站）上报告了 OpenAI 产品的问题。对于 Microsoft Outlook，此后不久该数字接近 4,600。两者在当天早些时候都达到了峰值。“ChatGPT Work 现在无法工作，”OpenAI 的 ChatGPT 帐户在 aposton X 中写道。“对此感到抱歉，我们正在努力修复！”

7 月，OpenAI 推出了 ChatGPT Work，这是一款与 Anthropic 的 Claude Cowork 直接竞争的企业代理。该代理旨在帮助员工承担更多“雄心勃勃的任务”，例如创建精美的幻灯片、网络应用程序、表格、文档以及执行其他复杂项目。

微软于 2019 年向 OpenAI 投资了第一笔 10 亿美元，为这家软件巨头在人工智能领域提供了早期立足点，比 ChatGPT 推出早了三年。随着战略关系的加强，这项投资后来增加到 130 亿美元，但最近两家公司一直在多个战线展开竞争。

“我们已经确认，用户可能会遇到各种 Exchange Online 功能降级的情况，”微软通过其 365 状态帐户向 X 表示。 “我们正在审查服务遥测和诊断数据，以找出问题的根源。”

title: Citadel 证券表示，随着历史上艰难的月份开始，股票的风险回报前景变得越来越糟
content:
众所周知，9 月份是股市最糟糕的月份，标准普尔 500 指数的平均月回报率最低。再加上目前全年最便宜的期权价格，在股市购买保护的风险回报看起来很有吸引力。

这是 Citadel 证券股票和股票衍生品策略主管 Scott Rubner 的观点，他周一写信给客户，表示标准普尔 8 月份创下历史新高的看涨格局正在发生变化。

“这不是我们长期建设性股票观点的变化。这是近期风险/回报的变化，”Rubner在一份策略报告中写道，指出收益日历、回购前景、季节性和零售交易模式是谨慎的原因。

“总的来说，它们改变了近期的不对称性，”鲁布纳说。 “随着下行催化剂变得越来越多，上行催化剂变得越来越不明显。”

标准普尔 500 指数本月盘中创下 7,816.70 点的历史新高，自 7 月底到 8 月第一周上涨近 7%。此后，随着芝加哥期权交易所波动率指数 (VIX) 衡量的波动率上周跌至 14.1——全年最低水平，该基准指标横向走低。

根据芝加哥期权交易所的数据，与指数波动率相比处于历史高位的单只股票波动率也有所下降，并援引了该交易所 VIXEQ 指数的利差——该指数衡量标准普尔 500 强 50 强的隐含波动率。同样，根据芝加哥期权交易所 (Cboe) 的数据，景顺信托 QQQ 衡量的纳斯达克 100 指数与 SPY 之间的价差从 6 月份的历史最高点降至一年来最低的 20%。

“随着对人工智能交易的担忧消退，强于预期的科技股盈利（正如上周 NVDA 所见）帮助压缩了科技股的波动性风险溢价，”芝加哥期权交易所衍生品市场情报主管 Mandy Xu 写道。周一早上的说明。

因此，根据 Citadel 的鲁布纳的说法，下行保护的成本并不高。

根据鲁布纳的说法，从历史角度来看，9 月不仅仅是艰难的时期。这也是 Citadel 追踪的零售交易商一年中购买活动最疲软的月份。自 2019 年以来，标准普尔指数下跌期间的平均零售净买入量约为平均水平的一半。

鲁布纳还写道，随着企业回购股票的禁售期在 9 月 12 日左右加速，企业回购将会放缓。

“投资者正在进入一个宏观事件更加频繁的时期，同时支付的保护溢价相对较少，”鲁布纳表示。

title: 美国袭击伊朗后股市下跌，但华尔街即将迎来胜利之月：实时更新
content:
Stocks fell on Monday after the U.S. and Irantraded firefor the first time in a month, though the major averages were still pacing to close out August with gains.

TheS&P 500slipped 0.5%, as did theNasdaq Composite. TheDow Jones Industrial Averagetraded 361 points, or 0.7%, lower, dragged down by losses inGoldman SachsandAlphabet.

On Sunday, U.S. Central Command confirmed to MS NOW that the U.S. struck two rocket launchers on Iran's Larak Island.

Sunday's attack was the first publicly acknowledged U.S. strike on Iranian positions since late July, with Iranian state media reporting that Tehran had attacked U.S. bases in Jordan in retaliation.

Oil prices jumpedafter the hostilities resumed.U.S. West Texas Intermediate oiltraded more than 2% higher at above $85 per barrel, while global benchmarkBrent crude oil futureswere up more than 2% at above $90 a barrel.

Longer-dated Treasury yields rosealongside oil prices Monday, adding to the downbeat sentiment in equities.

While Tom Hainlin of U.S. Bank Asset Management noted that oil's current levels are "a little high," the latest advance shouldn't be significantly damaging.

"The world's got enough oil for what it needs, and $80 to $90 is not so restrictive that it collapses the economy," the firm's national investment strategist said. "Today's indication just puts us at the high end of that range, but it doesn't change our outlook for the consumer, for business, for AI, manufacturing reshoring or continued electrification of the economy."

If oil climbs above $100 a barrel, then that may start to get "pretty prohibitive," he added.

Heightened tensions in the Middle East have contributed to choppy trading in August, but Wall Street is currently on track for a month of broad gains, led by the tech sector.

The Dow is up more than 1% month to date, putting the index on track for its fifth consecutive monthly advance. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq were headed for their first one-month increases since May, up about 2% and 3%, respectively. Both the S&P 500 and Dow also reached all-time highs earlier in August.

Tech led the charge this month, with artificial intelligence-linked stocks outperforming. The S&P 500 tech sector is up nearly 6% for the month.Nvidiahas climbed more than 9%, whileMicrosoftandMicron Technologyadvanced 10% and 15%, respectively.

To be sure, August has still been a turbulent month, as inflation fears sent Treasury yields to multi-year highs. The Treasury Department tried to stem the rout by saying itwould increase debt repurchases, but yields along the long end of the curve remain elevated. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warshalso said Fridayhe's worried about inflation, noting that, "while this summer's [inflation] readings were better than expected, they do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved."

Investors will get more insight into the state of the economy this week, with the August jobs report due Friday morning. Monthly manufacturing and services sector data is also on deck.

Traders will also be watching for developments out of Asheville, North Carolina, where ameeting of the Group of 20 finance ministersis taking place.

The stock market still has room to broaden beyond AI-related names into more cyclical areas, but warned that the outlook depended heavily on a continued soft landing, according to Scott Chronert, head of U.S. equity strategy at Citi Research.

"All in all, the balance which Mr. Warsh seems to be bringing to the Fed process appears reasonable, and we look forward to more from the Fed's task forces," Chronert wrote in his Friday note.

However, he said Citi's broadening call remains dependent on "some combination of lower oil prices, resultant lesser inflation pressure, and, ultimately, room for the Fed to react more dovishly to mixed labor trends."

Chronert said Citi would like to seeWTI crudefall back below $80 a barrel along with the10-year Treasuryyield move lower as the Fed provides some relief on rates.

"Confidence in soft-landing economic conditions remains critical to the broadening playbook, in our view, and this still appears to be the appropriate backdrop," he said.

A 6% annual appreciation in the Chinese yuan relative to the dollar is pulling down estimates for iPhone price hikes and their effect on the company's gross margins, according to investment bank Jefferies.

The potential hikes on the higher storage units of the Apple mobile phone could be 5 to 8 percentage points lower than previous estimates, analysts said in a Monday note to clients.

Those units account for "only 2% - 3% of the vol but the original prices likely yield higher [gross margins]," Edison Lee at Jefferies wrote to clients.

Check out some of the companies making the biggest moves midday:

Apple'slead for its App Store and events has stepped down from his role, Bloomberg reported on Monday.

Citing people familiar with the matter, Bloomberg added that Schiller will remain at the company and will work on unnamed initiatives.

Schiller's role change comes just before John Ternus is set to take over from Tim Cook as CEO of the consumer technology giant on Tuesday. Shares hit their lows of the session and were off about 2% after the report.

While theS&P 500was under pressure on Monday, falling 0.5% in midday trading thanks in part to a decline in utility stocks likeEdison International,Teslashares stood out with a gain of around 5%.

Ulta Beautywas another winner on Monday, with shares rising roughly 4%.

California-based utility providers headed for their worst day in several years on Monday.

Edison Internationalcratered more than 22%, which would mark its largest one-day decline since 2001.PG&Eshares plunged around 19% in midday trading, on track for their worst day since 2020.

Monday's decline came after California lawmakers reportedly stopped Gov. Gavin Newsom's plan to insulate utility providers from lawsuits by insurers over wildfires.

Energy is the only S&P 500 sector in positive territory on Monday morning.

The group was up about 2%, putting its gain this month at more than 6%.

Among the remaining 10 sectors, communication services and utilities were the two biggest laggards, falling 1.9% and 1.6%, respectively. The two are pacing for a monthly loss of 1.5% and 5.6%.

Federal Reserve ChairKevin Warshexpressed confidence in the U.S. economy during brief remarks Monday morning at the G20 conference.

"As I show up today, 100 days into my tenure, a comment that I made in Jackson Hole a day or two ago is that secular stagnation seems like a description of a past long ago. The new period is one of secular growth," Warsh said, referring to his Friday presentation at the Fed's annual symposium in Wyoming.

The central bank leader added that the current climate is "one of a global investment surge," echoing a theme he has sounded repeatedly over the past several months of artificial intelligence spurring cash flows towards business growth.

The three major averages began Monday's session in the red.

The S&P 500 fell 0.2% just after the opening bell, along with the Nasdaq Composite. The Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 207 points, or 0.4%.

With the last regular session of August about to kick off, here's how the three leading U.S. indexes have fared month to date:

TheRussell 2000 indexis also pacing to finish the month higher, having climbed 1.4% so far.

In markets as in movies, suspense builds through the slow, quiet scenes of the second act.

The stock market is doing just enough, through slim trading volumes and narrow index trading ranges, to escape August with its uptrend intact.

The S&P 500 is within half a percent of where it closed three weeks ago. It has slouched and equivocated in the two weeks since it hit the last record high just above 7800.

But the index has stayed within 2% of the peak, the pullbacks so far halting a handful of points above what had been the top of the former multi-month range.Read more.

Check out the companies making the biggest moves premarket:

Aonagreed to pay private equity giant KKR $17 billion for USI Insurance Service, the companies confirmed Monday.

The deal is "expected to deliver $395 million in annual run-rate net adjusted EBITDA impact from revenue and cost synergies," they said in a release.

"Combining with USI will establish the premier U.S. middle-market platform, deepen our context advantage and position Aon to accelerate organic growth. Building on the success of our acquisition of NFP, USI will substantially enhance our middle-market footprint," Aon CEO Greg Case said in a statement.

Aon and KKR shares were flat in the premarket.

Short-term government borrowing costs in various markets reached multi-year highs on Monday, as fresh U.S.-Iran combat fueled inflation fears.

The resumption of hostilities added to fears around inflation and interest rate hikes that were stoked by an unexpectedly hawkish speech from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh at the Jackson Hole symposium on Friday.

The yield onJapan's 2-year government bondtouched a 31-year high on Monday, whileGermany's 2-year bundyield was trading at its highest level since July 2024. France's2-year government bondyield rose to its highest since April 2024.

Bond prices move inversely to yields.

Bonds at the short end of the curve saw a broad sell-off across Europe, with short-term government borrowing costs also rising in theU.K., Spain, Portugal, Poland and Switzerland.

title: 由于新的中东袭击推高油价，抵押贷款利率飙升至 2025 年 6 月以来的最高水平
content:
伊朗战争重新爆发敌对行动后，油价上涨推高了债券收益率，抵押贷款利率也随之走高。

据《抵押新闻日报》报道，30年期固定贷款平均利率周一上涨6个基点至6.87%。这是自 2025 年 6 月以来的最高水平。自周四以来已上涨 12 个基点，并且在过去两个月中已上涨超过 30 个基点。

“虽然从技术上讲，利率处于一年多以来的最高水平，但它们并没有出现令人惊讶的新势头，”《抵押新闻日报》首席运营官马修·格雷厄姆 (Matthew Graham) 表示。 “相反，这更多的是由通常的嫌疑人推动的缓慢磨难：通胀预期、债券发行增加和经济弹性。所有这三个因素在未来至少都会受到一些变化的影响。”

人们原本预计今年利率会下降，但与伊朗的战争及其导致的油价上涨颠覆了这一预期。战争爆发前一天，即 2 月底，30 年期固定利率为 5.99%。

从这个角度来看，对于购买价值 45 万美元（约为全国中位数）的房屋的人来说，如果支付 30 年期固定抵押贷款 20% 的首付，那么今天每月还本金和利息将为 2,363 美元。这比 2 月底时每月多出 207 美元。

CNBC 与戴安娜·奥利克 (Diana Olick) 进行的房地产游戏为房地产投资者提供了新的和不断变化的机会，每周发送到您的收件箱。

立即订阅此处即可访问。

这只是付款。当利率上升时，有资格获得抵押贷款的借款人就会减少，因为这会改变贷方安全借贷所依赖的债务与收入比率。

这是在房价上涨的基础上出现的，由于供应不足，目前该国某些地区的房价似乎再次加速上涨。

根据最新的 S&P Cotality 数据，在全国范围内，6 月份的房价同比上涨 1.5%，而 5 月份的涨幅为 1.2%。凯斯-席勒房价指数。

“由于潜在买家的融资成本居高不下，当前的房主仍然不愿意放弃前几年获得的低抵押贷款利率，”标普道琼斯指数大宗商品副总监丽贝卡·考夫曼 (Rebecca Kaufman) 在新闻稿中表示。

title: 特朗普表示，反对人工智能数据中心的美国社区最终可能会“落后和贫穷”
content:
总统唐纳德·特朗普周一抨击了反对新数据中心的社区，共和党人在 11 月中期选举前面临选民对这些项目的强烈反对。

特朗普在《真相社会》帖子中写道，“美国各地的社区不想要数据中心的唯一原因是他们希望最终变得落后和贫穷。”

“如果他们想要成功和富有，那么各地的税收和就业机会都要低得多总统说。

“好消息是，还有很多其他地方想要它们。如果我们扼杀了金鹅，你们只能怪中国自己。事实上，他们不敢相信这一切正在发生！”

特朗普的帖子是在全国共和党参议院委员会发布备忘录警告“如果选民的看法”之后发布的。 NRSC 表示，该州的私人民意调查显示，在填补副总统 JD 万斯空出席位的剩余任期的特别选举中，共和党参议员乔恩·赫斯特德 (Jon Husted) 与民主党挑战者谢罗德·布朗 (Sherrod Brown) 处于“不相上下”状态。

5 月，盖洛普表示，3 月份进行的一项调查发现，“十分之七的美国人反对构建数据” 8月28日，Wolfe Research发布报告称，“在过去一个月左右的时间里，几乎每次与投资者会面时，我们都会被问到：选民对数据中心的强烈反对将如何发展？”

“反对的速度和规模确实令人惊叹——我们从未见过这样的情况，”报告称。 “过去 12 个月，跨党派对本地数据中心 (DC) 建设的净支持率下降了 60 个百分点。”

即将举行的中期选举将决定哪个政党控制国会两院。共和党在众议院以微弱优势占据多数，在参议院以 53 比 47 占据多数。

AI 数据中心拥有用于训练和运行 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 等公司开发的人工智能模型的计算设备。

急于建设数据中心的做法在美国各地社区引发了强烈反对，反对者对电力成本、电力需求、用水和其他当地影响表示担忧。

在 8 月 18 日的报告中在备忘录中，NRSC 警告说，美国人对数据中心的“当前看法是负面的”，因为它详细说明了这个问题如何影响俄亥俄州参议院的竞选。

“私下民意调查一直是一致的：当选民听到布朗的立场和他的记录时，赫斯特德退缩了。这仍然是这场竞选的路径，”备忘录说。 “新的成分（和新的问题）是数据中心。

NRSC 表示，“俄亥俄州是建设这些人工智能工厂的领导者之一。布朗已将其反对它们作为反对 Husted 的运动的核心。布朗正在使用它，因为它有效。”

“在这场竞赛中，数据中心比任何其他事情都更重要，是挂在 Husted 脖子上的锚。如果他输了并且数据中心受到指责，全国各地的政治家都会注意到 - 他们不会接近下一个。”

title: 安德鲁·贝利 (Andrew Bailey) 警告 G20 人工智能可能导致全球经济衰退
content: 图片来源，路透社，露丝·科默福德 (Ruth Comerford) 2小时前发布 英国央行行长警告G20财长，人工智能可能导致全球经济低迷，并对金融系统构成重大网络安全风险。安德鲁·贝利表示，人工智能行业增长的任何崩溃都可能导致波及全球的“未来市场调整”。在周一致美国财长的公开信中，他表示，世界各地的公司应该为“涉及本月早些时候，包括谷歌、微软、Anthropic 和 OpenAI 在内的 100 家公司敦促各国和团体在人工智能强大到足以超越它们之前加强网络防御。贝利告诉 G20 财长，股市高价、投资者借贷增加以及资金日益集中于少数主要科技公司，可能会放大未来的市场调整。杠杆率与高估值和市场集中度相互作用，特别是人工智能（AI）公司和超大规模企业之间日益增加的交叉投资，这可能会放大未来的市场调整。”他表示。贝利呼吁金融安全负责人制定“适当的措施，支持在全球范围内安全、负责任的模型发布和部署”。几个月前，英国财政大臣约翰·希利 (John Healey) 宣布设立 1 亿英镑基金，旨在支持英国人工智能初创企业。这是政府增强国家“主权人工智能”能力、开发本土人工智能技术以确保英国不依赖国外服务的努力的一部分。大臣们希望看到企业争夺资金，以帮助应对诸如削减 NHS 和医疗服务等候名单等挑战。英国政府发言人表示，其新成立的人工智能经济研究所正在与国际合作伙伴合作，“就人工智能如何改变世界各地的经济建立更强有力的共识。”该发言人表示，“该研究所是同类中第一个由政府支持的机构，专注于人工智能的经济影响，帮助政策制定者了解随着技术的快速发展，人工智能对增长、生产力、就业和公共服务意味着什么。”银行和金融中心。图片来源，盖蒂图片社图片说明，安德鲁·贝利希望负责金融安全的人员制定“适当的措施来支持安全和负责任的模型发布”。今年夏天，OpenAI、Anthropic 和 Meta 都展示了他们的人工智能工具做了他们不应该做的事情，一些人工智能代理甚至冒充真人以克服安全障碍。贝利领导的金融稳定委员会是一个全球监管机构，负责监督财政部官员、银行和证券监管机构。其中包括来自美国、英国、法国、德国、加拿大、日本、澳大利亚、中国和沙特阿拉伯的官员。相关主题人工智能更多关于这个故事的信息，警告顶级科技公司，网络安全的时间已经不多了发布于3天前，人类人工智能使用虚假个人资料来瞄准黑客，然后隐藏证据发布于8月5日，OpenAI代理之间的意外聊天导致了Hugging Face黑客攻击发布于4天前

title: G20 金融会议实时更新：Bessent、Warsh 发表讲话
content:
财政部长斯科特·贝森特和美联储主席凯文·沃谢尔将于周一在北卡罗来纳州阿什维尔举行的 20 国集团财长会议上发表讲话。

国际金融领导人、央行行长和其他高级官员的会议召开之际，世界经济正处于一个不稳定的时刻，因为唐纳德·特朗普总统发动了伊朗战争，美国债务激增，通货膨胀问题持续存在。引发了全球不确定性。

为期两天的会议吸引了众多知名首席执行官，包括摩根大通的杰米·戴蒙和高盛的大卫·所罗门，他们都定于周一晚些时候发表讲话。

CNBC 正在华盛顿特区纽约市阿什维尔和新泽西州恩格尔伍德克利夫斯报道 G20 会议。

伊朗经济可能会崩溃，因为贝森特预测，最快几周内就会出现这种情况，同时坚称这不是与德黑兰取得突破的先决条件。

当被问及伊朗经济需要多长时间才能崩溃时，贝森特在新闻发布会上表示：“我们有封锁，我们将继续施加压力，我们已经在这里进行了很好的讨论。”

“我认为这可能会在几周或几个月内，”他说，但补充道，“经济不必崩溃……我们只需让这个政权清醒过来。”

贝森特在抵达 G20 会议时感谢欧盟“对经济放逐者行动的大力支持”。

欧盟委员会表示，它支持“通过额外的经济压力，包括通过美国领导的经济放逐行动”来实现这一目标的努力。

财政部阻止《纽约时报》、《华尔街日报》和彭博社的一些记者参加在阿什维尔举行的会议，并禁止美国最大、最有影响力的三个新闻编辑室进入。

title: OpenAI 广告业务增长强劲，年化收入达到 10 亿美元
content:
OpenAI 周一宣布，其广告业务年化收入已达到 10 亿美元，该公司将这一里程碑视为其“多元化商业模式”的证明。

这家人工智能公司正在为预计将进行的大规模 IPO 做准备，并面临着向投资者证明其 8520 亿美元估值合理性的压力。 OpenAI 周一表示，其广告业务已有大约 200 天的历史，建立在现有的收入引擎基础上，例如企业产品、消费者订阅和基于使用的应用程序编程接口。

OpenAI 于 2 月份开始在美国的 ChatGPT 聊天机器人中测试广告，这一决定既备受期待，又引起争议。数字广告长期以来一直是 Google 和 Meta 等其他大型科技公司的摇钱树，但 OpenAI 的举动遭到了其主要竞争对手 Anthropic 的嘲笑，这使得 OpenAI 的广告成为其首届超级碗活动的焦点。

ChatGPT 广告现已在 40 多个国家/地区推出，OpenAI 表示将于周一在印度、欧洲、中东和北非推出自助服务访问。聊天机器人内的广告针对的是 OpenAI 的 Go 订阅者及其免费套餐，该订阅者占其 10 亿周活跃用户的绝大多数。

OpenAI 周一表示，其广告有明确的标签，不会影响 ChatGPT 的答案。广告商无法访问用户的私人对话。

“我们下一阶段的增长将把 ChatGPT 广告带入更多市场，并引入更多格式、目标、购买选项和衡量功能，”OpenAI 在一份新闻稿中表示。 “我们还将探索企业在 ChatGPT 中以更原生的方式与消费者互动的新方式。”

—CNBC 的 Kate Rooney 对本报告做出了贡献

title: 怡安首席执行官表示，保险经纪公司寻求通过收购竞争对手 USI 来建立“一流的中间市场平台”
content:
保险经纪公司奥安周一宣布，将从私募股权公司 KKR 手中收购竞争对手 USI Insurance Services。

这笔 170 亿美元的交易将由怡安以新债提供资金，预计将在第四季度完成，但需获得监管部门的批准。

首席执行官格雷格·凯斯周一在 CNBC 的“Squawk Box”节目中表示，此次合并将建立“美国顶级保险公司”。

“这意味着我们将能够为服务不足的美国中端市场带来世界一流的解决方案，并……为美国 20 万家中端市场公司及其 4800 万名员工制定客户领导力的新标准，”他说。

Aon 的收购建立在该公司于 2024 年收购 NFP 的基础上，NFP 是另一家专注于中端市场平台的保险经纪公司。美国中型市场。

据宣布此项交易的新闻稿称，USI 是美国第十大保险经纪公司，该公司年收入超过 30 亿美元，拥有超过 10,500 名员工。

交易完成后，USI 首席执行官 Mike Sicard 将接任怡安总裁兼中型市场全球首席执行官。

“加入怡安代表着一个真正充满活力的团队我们公司的新篇章以及作为怡安联合平台一部分加速我们发展势头的机会，”Sicard 在新闻稿中表示。 “我们的公司拥有强大的单一公司文化，并坚定地致力于共同努力，为客户提供最好的能力。”

KKR 合伙人 Chris Harrington 在一份新闻稿中表示，怡安是支持环旭电子下一个增长篇章的理想合作伙伴。

怡安股价在周一盘前交易中下跌约 1%。 但尽管最初业绩下滑，凯斯表示，通过收购，公司现在能够以规模服务中间市场的机会，对股东来说具有巨大的价值潜力。

“这也许是我作为首席执行官 20 年职业生涯中见过的最伟大的一次，”他说。

title: 曼哈顿的豪华租赁市场蓬勃发展，单位每月价格达到10万美元
content:
本文的一个版本首次出现在 CNBC 与 Robert Frank 合作的 Inside Wealth 时事通讯中，该通讯是针对高净值投资者和消费者的每周指南。注册后即可直接收到您的收件箱。

根据经纪人的说法，富裕租房者的激增将曼哈顿的租金推向新纪录。

曼哈顿的中位租金在 7 月份创下了每月 5,000 美元的历史新高。根据 Street Matrix 市场总监 Jonathan Miller 撰写的《真实交易报告》。平均租金较一年前上涨 15%，达到 6,306 美元。

富裕的租户是增长的主要推动力。根据《Real Deal Report》，豪华租金（市场前 10%）的平均价格在过去一年中上涨了 35%，达到每月 17,464 美元。现在豪华租金的平均价格为每平方英尺 121 美元。

通常，租户是那些还买不起的人。在当今的市场上，拥有大量现金可购买的超级富有的纽约人正在选择租房。待售高端房产供应量创历史新低，导致许多人等待出租，直到找到梦想之家。另一些人则对曼哈顿转售价格的下跌或持平感到惊慌，这使得公寓的投资吸引力下降。

Bespoke Real Estate 的劳拉·克莱因 (Laura Klein) 表示：“这些人可以轻松买得起 2000 万美元、5000 万美元的豪宅。”她最近以每月 177,000 美元的价格代理了切尔西一套顶层公寓的租金。 “库存太少了。而且他们不想妥协。”

其他经纪人表示，纽约新兴的高价值第二套住房已导致许多富有的潜在买家转而租房。

“临时住所税公告后租金急剧上涨，表明一些潜在购买者可能已经选择了灵活性而非所有权，”The Corcoran 总裁兼首席执行官 Pam Liebman 表示集团。

富裕的纽约人涌入租赁市场，为大型租赁创造了一个新市场。根据 The Real Deal 的数据，今年迄今为止，月租超过 50,000 美元的公寓数量比 2025 年增加了一倍多，而月租超过 100,000 美元的公寓数量增加了七倍。

Klein 表示，所有超高端租赁都没有公开上市，而是通过高端经纪人的小型网络悄悄向富裕客户提供。她目前在翠贝卡 (Tribeca) 的租金为每月 175,000 美元，在上东区的租金为每月 95,000 美元。

“现在每月 100,000 美元的数字几乎是正常的，”克莱因说。 “这些租户想要交钥匙、独特、奖杯的房产。”

她说，豪华出租屋的业主不需要收入，但考虑到需求，他们会投机取巧。

“他们对我说，‘如果数字正确，我就会出租。’她说，这些房产如果上市，售价将高达数千万美元。

罗伯特·弗兰克 (Robert Frank) 撰写的《内部财富》时事通讯是高净值投资者及其服务行业的每周指南。

title: 美国与伊朗的升级表明华盛顿对进展缓慢的制裁感到失望
content:
The escalation in hostilities between the U.S. and Iran over the weekend shows the U.S. is running out of patience with the slower-moving sanctions approach, according to analysts.

U.S. forces destroyed two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island on Sunday, as the Islamic Republic prepared to fire mine-carrying rockets into the Strait of Hormuz, ending a month-long lull in direct fighting.

The strike was the first publicly acknowledged U.S. attack since late July. Iran responded within hours, firing eight missiles at the King Hussein and Al Azraq air bases in Jordan. Jordanian air defenses intercepted all eight, with no casualties, the government said.

Later Sunday,President Donald Trumpthreatened on social media to blow up Kharg Island, Iran's main oil-export hub, to "smithereens."

"Most of the war has been tactically focused rather than strategic from the outset," said Ian Ralby, a maritime security expert and president of Auxilium Worldwide. "The question, therefore, is: why this, why now?"

The sanctions campaign may not be hurting Iran's leadership fast enough for the U.S.'s liking, Ralby said. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessenttold Reuterson Sunday that he expects new sanctions on Iran weekly, particularly targeting banks, and that Washington intends to cut Tehran-linked institutions out of the dollar system entirely.

"It may be that the financial pressure was not curtailing Iranian behavior to the level the U.S. anticipated," Ralby said. Renewed Iranian military activity may also have threatened U.S. forces or interests in the region "at a sufficiently high level of gravity that the U.S. felt it necessary to strike Iranian territory once more."

The U.S. strike is likely an attempt to break a deadlock rather than a shift in policy, Ralby added. "The status quo has become somewhat stagnant, and I'm sure the U.S. would like to see that change," he said. But it is unlikely to alter "the continuation of the blockade, or the economic 'warfare' being used to try to pressure Iran."

Trump's threat against Kharg Island is likely to remain rhetorical. The terminal has absorbed dozens of strikes since the war began, with itsoil infrastructure deliberately spared.

"It is unlikely that the President of the United States will actually carry through on the threat to attack Kharg Island," Ralby said, noting the island also holds a historic early church that Iran has worked to preserve.

An attack "would be a destruction of cultural heritage as well as destruction of critical oil infrastructure, which would likely cause catastrophic environmental harm," he said. "Threatening it may seem appealing, but actually blowing it up should hold little appeal."

Rather than confronting U.S. forces head-on, Iran is more likely to retaliate through proxies and pressure on shipping and energy flows.

"The key to this conflict from the outset has been asymmetry," Ralby said. "The Iranians have demonstrated an ability to use limited actual force to inflict substantial, actual harm."

For instance, the Houthis, who control a large part of Yemen and have held sway over the approaches to the Bab el-Mandeb for the better part of a decade, entered the war weeks ago in support of Iran.

With the Houthis restricting navigation through the Bab el-Mandeb, the U.S. and its allies in the region could face a situation where the two major maritime chokepoints used to export the majority of the Gulf's petroleum products are "subject to manipulation by Iran and its partners," said Michael Ratney, senior adviser at the Center for Strategic & International Studies.

"We always assume that the Houthis and Iran are part of the same kind of group, but they're not," said Claudio Galimberti, chief economist at Rystad Energy. "They have worked in the past quite independently."

Somali piracy, dormant since 2013, has also returned as coalition navies concentrate on the Red Sea and Hormuz. At least five vessels are currently held, including a tanker seized off Al Mukalla on Aug. 20.

"Enhanced pressure on oil production, the energy market, and global shipping are likely to be the focal points for Iranian retaliation," Ralby said.

The military campaign remains the dominant force in oil prices. Flows through the strait reached roughly 7 million barrels a day last week via the Omani corridor under U.S. Navy escort, according to Galimberti's estimates, calling it "a very costly mechanism ... but it's working."

The strike on Larak threatens to reverse that recovery, injecting fresh uncertainty into commercial shipping through the waterway. "The expectation is that the flows in the next couple of days probably will be lower, and therefore you should expect the price increase for sure," Galimberti said.

title: 随着政府借贷成本接近 2008 年高点，法国正在成为主权债务问题的“典型”
content:
France's deteriorating public finances and political deadlock are becoming a growing concern for bond investors, with borrowing costs near financial-crisis-era highs as another difficult budget battle looms.

The European Union's second-largest economy has endured recurring political instability and mounting fiscal strain in recent years. It has repeatedly broken European Commission rules on budget deficits and debt limits, and successive prime ministers have beenoustedafter failed attempts at reform, spending cuts and tax rises to bring the situation under control.

France is subject to the EU'sexcessive deficit procedure, with the Council recommending that itend its excessive deficitby 2029 — but it has a long way to go.

EU treaties set reference values of 3% of GDP for government deficits and 60% for government debt. Last year, France's deficit reached 5.1% of GDP, while the debt-to-GDP ratio surpassed 115%.

The IMF projected in July that France's gross government debt would reach about 118.5% of GDP in 2026 and exceed 120% in 2027, remaining above that level through 2030.

At the same time, the economy is struggling to grow, contracting 0.2% quarter-on-quarter in the first three months of this year and stagnating in the second quarter.

The upheaval has caused acute stress in the country's bond markets, with French government bond yields rising dramatically over the past year — exacerbated by the U.S.-Iran war's impact on borrowing costs worldwide — giving France some of the highest government borrowing costs in the G7.

French 10-year government bond yields hit their highest level since 2008, above 4.13%, last week and remained near 4.1% on Friday. Bond yields and prices move in opposite directions.

The French National Assembly is ideologically fractured, leading to no-confidencevotes, government collapse anddeadlocksover the national budget.

France is expected to submit its 2027 budget plans to parliament by early October. Last year's budget led to a deadlock that saw Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu force the bill through parliament after months of delays.

Lecornu became the fifth person to hold the role in just two years when he was appointed in 2025. Hisresignationjust 27 days into the job, saying political discord had made it too difficult to build a workable government program. Lecornu wasreappointeddays after quitting.

Another source of uncertainty that's weighed on French bonds is the 2027 presidential election, where far-right candidate Marine Le Pen is currently the frontrunner to succeed Emmanuel Macron.

John Stopford, head of multi-asset income at Ninety One, told CNBC that swelling deficits and slowing growth have become a global problem in the wake of the Covid-19 pandemic, wars and successive energy crises, but France "stands out."

"It's not just a French problem, but you could argue that in many ways France is one of the poster child [countries]," he said on a call. "So I don't think it's unique to France [but] France's public finances have been going in the wrong direction."

There is a broader challenge, he said, for developed governments to find a way to balance their books and bring debt onto a more sustainable path. Failing to do so is likely to lead to a "bond market revolt" at some point, Stopford added.

"I can see why people are concerned," he said of France. "It's not obvious how this ends in a good way."

The big uncertainty hanging over the OATs market is next year's presidential election, Stopford said.

During a candidate debate on Thursday, Le Pen said that the government "must drastically cut its spending," adding that she was "extremely concerned" about the trajectory of Paris's debt levels.

But Stopford told CNBC the market had been skeptical about whether Le Pen had much appetite for putting the public finances on a more sustainable footing.

"Clearly we may get a change of regime or policy priorities post May next year, but people doubt that there's much appetite for material fiscal consolidation," he said. "So yes, I think we might be building up to a crisis. I'm just not sure it's today."

Théophile Legrand, a rates strategist at Natixis CIB, told CNBC that his team already views OATs as "pre-stressed."

"What could delay a recovery is not only domestic politics, but also the broader macro backdrop," he said. "The market is not expecting France to return to a 3% deficit as early as 2027, but it does look for signs that the 2027 budget is consistent with a credible medium-term path for stabilizing public debt. That path is becoming harder to deliver. The war-related backdrop and higher long-end rates already complicate the fiscal equation, while this summer's heatwaves and wildfires add another layer of uncertainty."

The final months of this year and the first quarter of 2027 were the most likely window for another bout of volatility in OATs, Legrand added, as the budget debate and presidential dynamics become more closely intertwined.

"That said, we do not expect a repeat of the 2024/2025 shock pattern. OAT valuations already look materially stressed: our fair value model suggests OATs are around 15 basis points cheap even before adding any political premium, and our year-end forecast is around 75 basis points on the 10-year OAT-Bund spread if the budget is passed, versus around 80 basis points if it is not and France moves to a special budget law," he said.

April LaRusse, head of investment specialists at Insight Investment, said that despite increasingly bleak headlines related to the French economy, there is "surprisingly little sign that France is preparing for the kind of fiscal adjustment that its debt dynamics would seem to require."

"Growth expectations are being revised lower, debt is set to keep rising and bond yields are now at levels not seen since the financial crisis," she said. "Yet meaningful spending restraint remains politically difficult. With pension reform effectively on hold until after the 2027 election and parliament deeply fragmented, the government appears focused on maintaining political stability rather than tackling the underlying fiscal problem."

The question for investors now, she said, is whether policymakers can muster the political will to put public finances on a more sustainable path before market pressures intensify.

"French government bonds already trade more cheaply than their Italian equivalents, which would have been unthinkable not that long ago — but they could get even cheaper in a negative scenario," she said.

title: Jackson Hole分析师综述：沃什的讲话提高了加息机会，可能使美联储与财政部“产生分歧”
content:
美联储主席凯文·沃什在杰克逊霍尔会议上的讲话中出乎意料地强硬，提振了市场对下个月加息的预期。

周一金价下跌，亚洲股市下跌。根据芝商所的 FedWatch 工具，联邦基金期货交易者预计 9 月份加息 25 个基点的可能性为 60.4%，高于周五的 56% 左右。

以下是市场观察人士对 Warsh 讲话的评价：

“Warsh 主席在杰克逊霍尔的讲话对经济和前景的具体描述以及明显的鹰派倾向让我们感到惊讶，”德意志银行说。该公司继续预计美联储今年将加息 50 个基点，并在 9 月和 12 月联邦公开市场委员会会议上加息。

“对通胀风险的强调，加上 Warsh 对实现价格稳定的明确承诺以及他不愿预先承诺未来的政策行动，加大了今年政策紧缩的风险，尽管也可能是空谈而不采取行动，”大华银行在一份报告中表示。

“对近期通胀数据的敏感性是野村证券在一份报告中表示，“沃什在杰克逊霍尔经济研讨会上发表了强硬言论，强调了通胀目标的重要性，并暗示如果通货紧缩没有迅速发生，政策可能需要做出反应。”老虎经纪公司市场策略师 James Ooi 表示，沃什对美国经济表现强劲的评估“被视为减少了近期降息的理由”。 “强调 2% 的通胀目标可以被解读为加强美联储独立性和可信度的努力，让市场相信货币政策不会屈服于财政压力。”

Miller Tabak + Co. 首席市场策略师 Matthew J. Maley 认为，“加息仍然没有经验依据。”

“沃什似乎在大肆宣扬通胀，以便在总体措施不可避免地下降时，他可以声称自己能够抑制通胀。” Maley 表示，自上次 FOMC 会议以来，劳动力市场数据一直疲弱，而通胀数据好于预期。

Gavekal Research 在一份报告中表示，Warsh 重申短期利率应继续是货币政策的主要工具，这意味着他将继续缩短美联储资产负债表的平均期限。

“这似乎让美联储与美国财政部产生了分歧，美国财政部在 8 月初宣布将加大利率调整力度。 Gavekal 补充道，回购长期国债显然是为了防止长期收益率进一步上升。

Susquehanna 表示，“Warsh 承诺将通胀率恢复到 2% 的目标，并表示利率可能会进一步上升，从而走强美元并扭转部分贬值交易，8 月份金价曾因此上涨约 14%，为本世纪最强劲的月度涨幅。”

——CNBC 的 Joanna奥辛格为本报告做出了贡献。

title: 中国工厂活动连续第二个月萎缩，收缩幅度低于预期
content:
中国8月份制造业活动连续第二个月萎缩，尽管幅度低于市场预期，在增长失去动力的情况下，北京方面仍面临支持经济的压力。

国家统计局周一公布的数据显示，官方采购经理人指数为49.8，7月份为49.2，好于路透社调查的经济学家预测的49.6。

中国经济面临着越来越大的压力，第二季度经济增速放缓至 4.3%，为 2022 年底以来的最低增速，原因是内需疲软和房地产业长期低迷继续对经济活动构成压力。

今年下半年，经济萎靡不振进一步加深，消费者支出停滞，城市投资收缩加快，失业率上升。

7 月份零售销售和工业产出双双放缓，工业利润增速放缓出口是今年支撑经济增长的少数支柱之一，随着全球人工智能基础设施支出的繁荣提升了对中国制造科技产品的需求，出口缓冲了外部冲击带来的部分拖累。今年大部分时间出境货运量录得两位数增长。

经济学家预计，随着恶劣天气的消退和地方政府加快财政支出，今年剩余时间会有更好的增长。

经济学人智库高级经济学家徐天辰表示，由于政策制定者对城市投资崩溃越来越担心，北京可能会进一步加快财政支出。 “这应该会加快项目审批和资金拨付。”

徐说，但这种政策扩张的效果只会在下个月和第四季度变得更加突出，这表明内需复苏的初步迹象。

根据国家统计局的数据，8月份供需双双改善，跟踪生产和新订单的分项指数分别扩大至50.4和50.6。

新出口订单8 月份，制造业指数从上月的 49.6 反弹至 50.1，表明尽管全球经济经受住了中东长期动荡，海外需求仍出现复苏。

然而，原材料库存和就业分项指数均处于收缩区间，低于 50 关口。

高科技装备制造业的表现超过了更广泛的工厂部门。电子机械和设备、计算机通信设备行业的生产和新订单读数突破 53，而消费品生产则落后于 49。

总体而言，企业似乎预计“随着地方政府在今年剩余时间里加大支出，经济活动将得到提振”。凯投宏观 (Capital Economics) 中国经济学家 Nguyen Hoang Nam 表示。

工厂出厂价格分类指数的改善也表明通胀压力再次出现，部分原因是全球原油和金属价格上涨。

精点资产管理公司总裁张志伟表示，“大宗商品价格的上涨可能使上游制造业的一些企业受益，”尽管价格上涨是由供应限制推动的，因为需求仍然疲软。

追踪建筑和服务活动的非制造业指标在 8 月份保持在 49% 不变，尽管建筑业分类指数下降了 0.1 个百分点。 46.9%。

在服务类别中，批发、零售和资本市场服务活动萎缩。

根据路透社的一项民意调查，私人RatingDog制造业PMI调查预计将显示工厂活动攀升至51，结果将于周二公布。该指标往往涵盖规模较小、出口导向型的企业，并且历来描绘出比官方 PMI 读数更为乐观的前景。

title: 美加贸易战五张图表
content: ByNadine Yusif,ÂSenior Canada ReporterÂandÂJessica Murphy,ÂCanada editorPublished27 minutes agoThe US and Canada appear no closer to resolving their ongoing trade dispute.Tensions have been simmering between the two neighbours since President Donald Trump returned to the White House just over 18 months ago, and unleashed a wide-ranging global programme of tariffs.Canada was one of the first countries the Trump administration hit with levies, and is one of two countries to respond with its own reciprocal measures.Currently, the US has hit Canada's key sectors of steel, aluminium, lumber and automobiles with tariffs, and last week imposed an additional 50% levy on about C$28bn ($20bn; Â£15bn) of Canadian goods.Canada has hit back with its own counter-tariffs on American goods, announcing on Tuesday what it calls a "dollar-for-dollar" and "strategic" retaliation designed to match the US tariffs.With no resolution in sight, how has this enduring trade war affected Canada and the US, and what could come next?Here are five charts to help break it all down.Trade war hits Ontario hardestThe tariffs and counter-tariffs have hit some states and provinces harder than others.In Canada, some provinces have been more exposed to US sectoral tariffs on steel, steel derivatives, aluminium, and autos and vehicle parts that don't comply with the current North American trade deal, known as the USMCA.Ontario, the most populous province with a significant manufacturing sector, has been hardest hit by the auto and steel tariffs.Several Ontario auto parts and assembly plants have announced layoffs and production cuts, and the province is estimated to have lost tens of thousands of manufacturing jobs since early 2025.Metal exports from Quebec - which produces steel, copper and aluminium - fell 36% between February 2025 and 2026, and there was a 3.6% drop in employment in the sector, according to data released in July.The Royal Bank of Canada estimates that Ontario and Quebec are the most impacted by US sectoral tariffs, while Newfoundland and Labrador, New Brunswick, Alberta, Saskatchewan and Prince Edward Island are the least exposed.Additional US tariffs on $20bn worth of Canadian goods that came into effect on 22 August are expected to impact all provinces in some way, though British Columbia, Quebec and Ontario will feel the brunt.Swing states in the cross hairsThe US economy is much larger and the impact of Canada's counter-tariffs won't be as stark.But some states will feel the pain of Canada's retaliation more than others, with tariffs levied on C$28bn worth of US goods from steel to furniture, cosmetics and toilet paper, as of 8 September.According to data by Statistics Canada, the swing state of Ohio will be hardest hit, with C$3.2bn - or 12% - of its exports soon to be tariffed by Canada, followed by Illinois and Pennsylvania.For Ohio, it's the tax on steel that will particularly hurt, as well as the tax on laundry machines. In Illinois, where farm equipment giant John Deere is based, it will be the new tariffs on farm and construction equipment.Derek Holt, an economist with Scotiabank, noted that Canada's counter-tariffs appear to be "very deliberately oriented" towards some swing states that could decide the US balance of power in the upcoming midterm elections.From the lowest tariff rates to one with the packPrime Minister Carney has assured Canadians that, despite the high-profile trade fight, they face some of the lowest US tariff rates compared to other countries.But with the latest 50% tariffs imposed on a range of Canadian goods, the average effective US tariff rate on Canada is now higher than Mexico's, and is approaching the rate faced by others like the UK and Vietnam.An average effective tariffs rate reflects the average tariff paid across all imports.According todata by the Royal Bank of Canada,external, the average effective US tariff rate on Canada in June was 2.9% - the lowest among major US trade partners. It has now nearly doubled to 5.7%.By comparison, the US effective tariff on the UK is 6.2%. China still faces the highest US tariffs at an average of around 20.5%.Canada's exports are going elsewhereCanada, by the happenstance of being neighbours with the world's largest economy, is hugely reliant on US trade.Their proximity - and free trade agreements in place since the 1990s - has allowed the two countries to develop one of the world's most deeply economically integrated trading relationships.The US buys more than 70% of Canadian exports, and is a top US trading partner alongside Mexico and China.But the tariff fight has already started to shift Canadian businesses to other markets. Carney has pledged to double Canada's non-US exports over the next decade.Bank of Canada statistics suggest that Canadian firms are exporting more to countries other than the US since Trump's return to the White House in January 2025.Some businesses are adapting to find customers elsewhere.Matteo Sgaramella, who owns Toronto-based menswear clothing company Outclass, told the BBC he has started attending trunk shows in Paris instead of New York, helping him reach more customers in Europe."The reception has been amazing," he said, adding that some European stores are particularly enthused about supporting Canadian products due to the ongoing trade war with the US."We're kind of seen as the one country that's kind of standing up to the Americans right now," Sgaramella said.Other businesses, however, are struggling to diversify their trade, particularly in Ontario manufacturing sectors that are deeply integrated with the US.A recent report by the Canadian Chamber of Commerce pointed out three such regions in Ontario - Oshawa, London and Kitchener-Cambridge-Waterloo - as being particularly vulnerable."These cities remain heavily tied to the US market, while growth in exports outside the US has been limited or insufficient to offset broader weakness in trade activity and local economic conditions," the report said.While some businesses are lagging, foreign direct investment into Canada hit C$96.8 billion in 2025, the highest inflow of capital to the Canadian economy since 2007.Canada's economy also strongly rebounded in the second quarter of 2026 to 3.3% growth in the country's GDP, thanks to a jump in exports and domestic investment.These latest figures have warded off recession concerns, at least for now.Carney is hoping to attract even more investment. In September, his government will host the first-ever Canada Investment Summit, bringing major investors, CEOs and business leaders to Toronto for two days.Fewer jobs and less disposable incomeOn both sides of the border, tariffs have hit jobs and disposable income.According to an analysis commissioned by Canadian American Business Council (CABC), if the US and Canada allow the USMCA to fail, there would be tens of thousands of jobs lost, primarily in the manufacturing industries directly affected by tariffs and that are highly reliant on the US market.Around 55,000 manufacturing jobs have already been lost in Canada from January 2025 to January 2026, according to Bank of Canada data.Not all figures are bad, however, as employment has steadily risen in Canadian sectors that are not vulnerable to US tariffs.But there is a risk of further Canadian job losses due to the recent 50% tariffs imposed by the Trump administration.Calgary-based economist Trevor Tombe estimates that a total of 90,000 jobs across Canada could be lost if these new US tariffs persist.In the US, the non-partisanCenter for American Progress estimates,externalthat Trump's "Liberation Day" tariffs, placed last year on dozens of America's trade partners, have also led to tens of thousands of jobs lost manufacturing, transportation and warehousing sectors.Even for those whose jobs remain secure, the tariffs have meant higher sticker prices on everyday items.The US-basedTax Foundation estimates,externalthat an American household could pay $840 more on average this year due to Trump's tariffs on a number of nations, including Canada.Canada's counter-tariffs are much more targeted and are designed to limit the impact on Canadian consumers, but economists say businesses will likely now pay more to manufacture goods, as a bulk of the taxes will be applied on industrial supplies imported from the US.Related topicsCanadaUnited StatesTrump tariffsTrade war

title: 韩国美容巨头 APR 股价今年在美国 Costco 9 月上市前上涨 100%
content:
韩国美容公司 APR 的股价今年飙升近 100%，这家韩国美容公司迅速扩大在美国的业务。

APR 告诉 CNBC，其旗舰品牌 Medicube 将于 9 月进入美国 Costco 商店。 Medicube 的 Zero Pore Pad 2.0 是一款旨在清洁毛孔的护肤产品，将在该零售商的美国商店出售。

即将推出的这款产品标志着 APR 继去年 8 月在 Ulta Beauty、4 月在 Target 和 6 月在沃尔玛推出产品之后，最新进军美国主要零售商。

这家韩国美容公司于 2024 年在韩国基准 Kospi 上市，现在拥有市值约为 17.3 万亿韩元（125 亿美元），几乎是长期美容巨头爱茉莉太平洋的两倍，是 LG 生活保健的三倍多。

APR 在美国迅速扩张，美国已成为该公司的关键市场。第二季度北美销售额达到 3,763 亿韩元（2.73 亿美元），占总收入的 49%。

根据 APR 公司的数据，在 6 月 23 日至 26 日的 Prime Day 活动期间，Medicube 是亚马逊所有类别中搜索次数最多的词。

本月早些时候，APR 报告称，其第二季度收入较上年同期跃升 134.2%，达到 7,675 亿韩元。营业利润则增长134.5%，达到1906亿韩元。海外销售占总收入的 91.8%。

APR 正受益于美国更广泛的韩国美容热潮。根据韩国食品药品安全部的数据，韩国化妆品出口额预计在 2026 年上半年达到创纪录的 70 亿美元，同比增长 27.3%。美国是最大的目的地，占出口总额的 14.5 亿美元，占出口总额的 20.7%。

该公司将全年收入预测从约 2.1 万亿韩元上调至 3 万亿韩元，理由是美国市场的增长以及进一步全球扩张的潜力。 APR 副总裁 Shin Jae-ha 在公司第二季度财报电话会议上表示，今年美国销售额预计将达到约 1.3 万亿韩元。

APR 股价去年上涨了 360% 以上。

title: 喜马拉雅山灾害死亡人数接近 800 人，救援人员奋力抗击洪水和废墟
content:
Rescuers in Nepal and China raced on Sunday to find thousands of people missing after a glacier collapse unleashed a catastrophic mudslide across the Himalayas, as they faced challenging weather conditions and rising water levels.

Authorities said the death toll rose to nearly 800 on Sunday, with more than 3,000 people missing on both sides of the Nepal-China border after a torrent of ice, rock, mud and debris swept through mountain valleys and rivers on Wednesday, causing widespread devastation.

The Red Cross has estimated that more than 90,000 people are likely to have been affected by the disaster, which China has linked to the effects of climate change.

Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi told his Nepalese counterpart during a Saturday telephone call that the mudslide was their "most severe cross-border disaster" in recent years and that rescue operations had risen to an unprecedented level of difficulty and complexity, state broadcaster CCTV reported.

Nepal's disaster authority said 781 people had died, with 2,502 missing. On the Chinese side, authorities said 16 people were killed in Gyirong County and 546 were missing.

Beijing said 261 foreign nationals from 23 countries were unaccounted for in Tibet, near a key border crossing with Nepal.

The scale of the disaster has complicated rescue efforts across the rugged Himalayan terrain.

Local police in Nepal told Reuters that residents and rescue workers had moved to higher ground after the Trishuli River's water levels rose in recent hours following fresh rainfall, raising fears of additional flooding.

Rescue operations have been suspended several times since Friday because of bad weather and concerns that a lake formed across the Nepal-China border by the disaster could trigger fresh flooding after it began overflowing into Nepal's Lhende Khola and Trishuli Rivers.

CCTV reported that the lake threatening downstream areas had been largely drained by Saturday evening. But drones detected a landslide late on Saturday that is 2.8 kilometers (1.7 miles) downstream of the lake, forming a new dam and a fresh pool of water.

In Nepal, rescue efforts have increasingly focused on five hydropower projects inundated by the floods, including the Upper Trishuli complex, where authorities said on Friday they received information that around 350 people could be trapped inside a tunnel. About 10,000 Nepali troops have been deployed alongside specialist teams from China and India.

Nepal's military airlifted heavy machinery to the remote site on Sunday and rescuers reached the entrance of one tunnel, beginning to clear debris blocking access. Authorities said teams carrying oxygen supplies and cameras would enter once access was secured.

"It's very tough because there's a lot of debris and we cannot blast things to make our way through," said Dharam Raj Uprety, chief of Nepal's national disaster management authority.

Lok Bahadur Chhetri, a spokesperson for Nepal's foreign ministry, said Nepal required international assistance in specialized areas, including tunnel rescue operations, DNA testing, refrigerated storage for bodies and forensic identification of decomposed remains.

Days after desperate relatives moved between hospitals, morgues and relief centers searching for loved ones, authorities in Nepal began mass burials of hundreds of unidentified victims whose bodies had started to decompose.

In Chitwan district, about 200 km (125 miles) from the disaster zone, authorities dug hundreds of graves in a forest at Devghat for bodies swept downstream from the flood-hit Rasuwa region.

"We were left with no other option," said Ganesh Aryal, chief district officer of Chitwan. "Our concern was the risk to public health posed by the rapid decomposition of the bodies."

Authorities buried 96 unidentified bodies on Saturday and planned to bury more than 100 others on Sunday as recovery teams continued retrieving victims from rivers and debris. DNA samples were collected and burial sites carefully documented in the hope that families may still be able to identify relatives later.

"Of the bodies we have recovered so far, more than half are beyond recognition," police officer Anil Thapa told Reuters.

"Many have no visible faces. In some cases, only hands or legs remain; in others, only parts of the body are available."

The flood was "caused by glacier instability under the long-term effects of global warming," CCTV reported, saying it was a "new and prominent feature of cryosphere disasters" on the Tibetan plateau.

The mudslide from the Nepalese side took six to seven minutes to reach the Gyirong border crossing, CCTV said, citing the findings of Chinese scientists. Dramatic surveillance footage shared worldwide showed torrents of water and debris engulfing buildings while people tried to flee.

The state-run TV channel reported China has mobilized more than 2,100 rescue workers and allocated at least 220 million yuan ($32.7 million) to support relief efforts and has been airdropping equipment and supplies to frontline rescuers, while its soldiers used life-detection equipment to look for the missing.

title: U.S. plans to sanction another bank in effort to clamp down on Iran transactions: Bessent
content:
The Trump administration plans to impose sanctions on another bank this week to clamp down on Iran transactions, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Sunday.

Bessent spoke with The Associated Press ahead of Group of 20 meetings in Asheville, North Carolina, where he will meet individually with his counterparts from the world's major and developing economies to encourage participation in the economic isolation of Iran.

"This is going to be financial violence if we have to," Bessent said in the interview. "We are showing people that we know who you are, you know who you are, and this has got to stop."

Bessent had recently announced a new campaign to push countries that still do business with the already heavily sanctioned Islamic Republic to sever their financial ties or face retaliation from the United States.

The Treasury Department on Fridaymoved to sanctionthe United Arab Emirates branch of an Egyptianbankover its financial ties to Iran.

Treasury intends to revoke the access of Banque Misr UAE to U.S. financial institutions, the department said in a statement.

The action comes four days after Bessent launched "Operation Economic Outcast," asanctions campaignthat aims to sever all of Iran's economic ties around the world.

—CNBC contributed to this report.

title: U.S. strikes Iranian rocket launchers near Strait of Hormuz
content:
U.S. forces struck two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island on Sunday after the military said Revolutionary Guard forces were preparing rockets carrying sea mines for launch into the Strait of Hormuz, U.S. Central Command confirmed to MS NOW.

"I can confirm that earlier today U.S. forces struck two Iranian launchers on Larak Island. Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces were observed preparing to launch rockets with sea mines into the Strait of Hormuz," Navy Capt. Tim Hawkins, a U.S. Central Command spokesperson, said in a statement.

"Last week, CENTCOM completed clearing sea mines from the strait's international shipping routes. U.S. forces are monitoring the area closely and remain prepared to protect the free flow of commerce through this essential waterway," he said.

Sunday's attack was the first publicly acknowledged U.S. strike on Iranian positions since late July, according to The Associated Press. The war has entered its sixth month and sharply disrupted vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global energy shipments.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards acknowledged the strikes, reported casualties, and said they would respond, AP reported. The group reportedly said they would respond.

This story is developing. Please check back for updates.

title: 特朗普推动的自由加油站出售天然气，经销商称未付款
content:
自由燃油网络早在 7 月份就成为全国头条新闻，当时唐纳德·特朗普总统称赞该加油站连锁店以大幅折扣价格销售燃油。佐治亚州一家燃料供应商提起诉讼，声称通过网络销售的部分天然气从未付款。

在 8 月 19 日提起的联邦诉讼中，盖恩斯维尔的曼斯菲尔德石油公司表示，商人 Syed Kazmi 和他的公司 KRSM 在 5 月至 7 月期间从宾夕法尼亚州的一个供应终端获得了超过 110 万加仑的燃料。诉讼称，当曼斯菲尔德在 7 月份寄出价值约 400 万美元的燃油发票时，该账单尚未支付。

诉讼进一步指控 KRSM 将部分燃油出售给自由燃油网络中的加油站。该诉讼没有将 Freedom Fuel Network 列为被告，也没有指控该公司有不当行为。

7 月初，Freedom Fuel Network 在宾夕法尼亚州和新泽西州的 25 个加油站以每加仑 3.47 美元的价格出售汽油，以纪念唐纳德·特朗普总统作为第 47 任总统的地位，这比该地区其他加油站的价格大幅折扣。

特朗普宣称此举证明美国消费者很快就会在加油站看到“创纪录的低价”。尽管美国石油价格上涨，但燃油价格仍然上涨。特朗普于 7 月 1 日在 Truth Social 上发帖称，“7 月 3 日，自由燃料网络将降低大费城地区 25 个“自由燃料”站的汽油价格。“这家零售商正在带头，其他人也应该效仿。他们这样做是因为他们热爱美国。”

曼斯菲尔德声称，未支付的燃料至少帮助实现了部分折扣诉讼称：“KRSM 之所以能够以如此低的价格出售此类燃料并获得如此高的知名度，是因为它从未向原告支付此类燃料的费用。”

8 月 28 日，负责此案的法官部分批准了曼斯菲尔德的初步禁令请求，并根据法庭记录，命令被告维持至少 275 万美元的银行账户余额。

该诉讼没有具体说明多少金额价值 400 万美元的汽油流向 Freedom Fuel 站，或表明这些加油站是否与 KRSM 或 Kazmi 有关系。

据 Politico 报道，新泽西州至少有 6 个 Freedom Fuel 加油站由被告 Syed Kazmi 的兄弟 Shamikh Kazmi 管理。

KRSM 的法律代表 Mauro Tucci 表示，此事归结为发票差异。

“KRSM 对本案中的指控提出异议。案件是关于曼斯菲尔德石油公司错误定价的燃料发票的会计纠纷，”他在给 CNBC 的电子邮件中说道。 “我们不会对这一悬而未决的诉讼发表进一步评论。” 白宫官员告诉 CNBC，政府与被告没有联系或打交道。 Freedom Fuel Network 没有回应 CNBC 的置评请求。
